reference.title: TLS encryption for Operator-managed PostgreSQL
reference.shortdesc: You can enable TLS encryption for Operator-managed PostgreSQL databases used by Red Hat Quay and Clair. Configure TLS through the overrides.tls fields on the postgres and clairpostgres components in the QuayRegistry custom resource.

note.p: This feature configures transport encryption for Operator-managed PostgreSQL connections. It is distinct from the managed tls component, which handles Red Hat Quay’s external HTTPS endpoint.

section.p: When TLS is enabled, the Operator configures PostgreSQL to accept encrypted connections and mounts the TLS certificates on the database pod. TLS is opt-in. Existing deployments continue to use unencrypted database connections until you explicitly enable it.

note.p: After you enable TLS, confirm that PostgreSQL reports ssl = on. Optionally verify that Red Hat Quay or Clair client sessions appear in pg_stat_ssl, or that the registry database URI includes an sslmode setting such as verify-full, depending on your Operator version and configuration.

section.p: You can enable TLS independently for the postgres and clairpostgres components.

entry.p: OpenShift Container Platform Service CA (default on OpenShift Container Platform)

When you set overrides.tls.enabled: true without a secretRef, the Operator uses the OpenShift Container Platform Service CA on clusters that support Routes. The Operator annotates the PostgreSQL Service with service.beta.openshift.io/serving-cert-secret-name and mounts the generated serving certificate.
On Kubernetes clusters without the OpenShift Container Platform Service CA, the Operator generates ECDSA P-256 certificates with a 10-year validity period when no secretRef is provided.

Reference a Secret containing ca.crt, tls.crt, and tls.key by using overrides.tls.secretRef.name. This format is compatible with cert-manager output. When the referenced Secret changes, the Operator reconciles the deployment.

note.p: This feature does not provide mutual TLS (mTLS) or automatic certificate rotation. To integrate with enterprise PKI or automate rotation, use secretRef with cert-manager or your own certificate management process.
